key_concepts: Friction is a force that opposes motion.
Friction acts in a direction opposite to an object's motion.
Rough surfaces produce more friction than smooth surfaces.
Objects slow down more quickly on rough surfaces than on smooth surfaces.
Static, sliding, rolling, and fluid friction are types of friction.
Gravity pulls objects toward Earth's center.
Gravitational pull is weaker on the Moon than on Earth.
Without air resistance, objects dropped from the same height hit the ground at the same ti
Free fall is falling without air resistance.
The Sun's gravitational pull keeps planets in their orbits.
Mass and weight are different concepts.
Friction can be reduced by waxing or oiling surfaces and increased by rubberized mats.
